- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows steady upward trend with no volatility, true outcome often reverses or drops sharply; cap forecast slope at 0.5% per day after 3 consecutive days of rise.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 2–5 days, especially if recent history shows volatility.  
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 20+ days of forecast shows steady increase, check for 10-day mean reversion signal (true outcome drops >2% from 10-day average).  
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.0 values, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 1–3% per day for next 5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong upward movement after model’s flat forecast, sentiment must be positive; if not, model is likely underestimating demand or policy impact.
